layout.metaDescription: Atelier Belli is the digital atelier of Ivan Lorenzana — full-stack developer crafting clean iOS apps and the web around them. Fingo, Savely, Mi Mezcal and more.

intro.heading: Introduction
intro.body: Welcome to Atelier Belli. We are committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit our website or use our mobile applications (such as Fingo, Savely, and Alisio). Please read this policy carefully. If you disagree with its terms, please do not access the site or our applications.

dataCollected.heading: Information We Collect
dataCollected.intro: We may collect information about you in a variety of ways. The information we may collect on the site or through our applications includes:

personalData.label: Personal Data:
personalData.body: Personally identifiable information — such as your name, shipping address, email address, and phone number — as well as demographic information such as your age, gender, hometown, and interests, that you voluntarily provide when you register on the site or our applications, or when you choose to participate in various activities related to the site and our applications, such as online chat and message boards.

derivedData.label: Derived Data:
derivedData.body: Information our servers collect automatically when you access the site or our applications, such as your IP address, browser type, operating system, access times, and the pages you viewed directly before and after accessing the site.

financialData.label: Financial Data:
financialData.body: Financial information — such as data related to your payment method (for example, a valid credit card number, card brand, expiration date) — that we may collect when you purchase, order, return, exchange, or request information about our services from the site or our applications.

mobileAppData.label: Mobile Application Data:
mobileAppData.intro: If you connect using our mobile application(s):

deviceInfo.label: Mobile Device Information.
deviceInfo.body: We may collect device information (such as your mobile device ID, model, and manufacturer), operating system, version information, and IP address.

geolocation.label: Geolocation Data.
geolocation.body: We may request access or permission to track location-based information from your mobile device, either continuously or while you are using our mobile application, in order to provide location-based services.

healthData.label: Health & Fitness Data (Alisio):
healthData.body: Our Alisio app reads heart rate, active energy, and workout data from Apple HealthKit, with your explicit permission, solely to calculate your heart-rate training zones and show your live training metrics on your Apple Watch and iPhone. This data, along with your training history, is stored only on your own devices. We do not transmit it to our servers, share it with third parties, or use it for advertising. Alisio requires no account and no personal data beyond what you choose to enter (age and resting heart rate) to calculate your zones.

dataUse.heading: How We Use Your Information
dataUse.intro: Having accurate information about you allows us to provide you with a smooth, efficient, and personalized experience. Specifically, we may use information collected about you through the site or our applications to:
items: Email you regarding your account or orders.
Fulfill and manage purchases, orders, payments, and other transactions related to the site and our applications.
Improve the efficiency and operation of the site and our applications.
Calculate your personal heart-rate training zones and display live training data within the Alisio app, processed entirely on your device.

dataSecurity.heading: Security of Your Data
dataSecurity.body: We use administrative, technical, and physical security measures to help protect your personal information. While we have taken reasonable steps to secure the personal information you provide to us, please be aware that no security measures are perfect or impenetrable, despite our best efforts.

privacyRights.heading: Your Privacy Rights
privacyRights.body: Depending on your location, you may have certain rights with respect to your personal information. For more information on how to exercise these rights, please visit our

children.heading: Children's Policy
children.body: We do not knowingly solicit information from or market to children under the age of 13. If you become aware of any data we have collected from children under 13, please contact us using the contact information provided below.

changes.heading: Changes to This Privacy Policy
changes.body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: If you have questions or comments about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at:
contact.name: Atelier Belli

favePrivacy.title: Fave Privacy Policy
favePrivacy.intro: Fave keeps your rankings on your device and in your personal iCloud account. That is the whole story, but here it is in detail:

collect.heading: What we collect: nothing
collect.body: Fave has no accounts, no analytics, no ads, no tracking, and no servers of our own. We never see your data.

dataLocation.heading: Where your data lives
dataLocation.body: Everything you write in Fave (your lists, entries, ratings, notes, and photos) is stored on your device and synced through your private iCloud database, which only your Apple ID can access. Apple's handling of iCloud data is described in Apple's own privacy policy. Deleting the app and its iCloud data removes everything; we keep no copies, because we never had any.

artwork.heading: Movie, show, and book artwork
artwork.tmdb: When you search for a movie or show, Fave queries The Movie Database (TMDB) and loads poster images from TMDB's servers. Those requests go directly from your device to TMDB and are subject to TMDB's privacy policy. Fave sends only your search text and standard network information; it never sends your rankings, notes, or photos to TMDB or anyone else.
artwork.openLibrary: When you search for a book, Fave queries Open Library and loads cover images from Open Library's servers. Those requests go directly from your device to Open Library and are subject to Open Library's privacy policy. Here too, Fave sends only your search text and standard network information; your rankings, notes, and photos never leave your device and your iCloud account.

children.heading: Children
children.body: Fave collects no data from anyone, including children.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.body: If this policy ever changes, the date above changes with it and the current version will always live at this URL.

privacyChoices.title: User Privacy Choices
privacyChoices.intro: At Atelier Belli, we respect your privacy and give you control over your personal information. Below are the choices you have regarding your data:

access.heading: Access to Your Information
access.body: You have the right to request a copy of the personal information we hold about you. You may do so by contacting us at ivanlorenzana@outlook.com.

correction.heading: Correction of Your Information
correction.body: If you believe that any information we hold about you is inaccurate or incomplete, please contact us as soon as possible. We will correct any information found to be inaccurate.

deletion.heading: Deletion of Your Information (Right to Erasure)
deletion.body: You may request the deletion of your personal information from our systems under certain circumstances — for example, if the data is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, or if you withdraw your consent (where processing is based on consent).

objection.heading: Objection to Processing
objection.body: You have the right to object to the processing of your personal information in certain situations, such as direct marketing. If you object, we will stop processing your personal information for those purposes unless we have compelling legitimate grounds for the processing that override your interests, rights, and freedoms, or for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims.

restriction.heading: Restriction of Processing
restriction.body: You may request that we restrict the processing of your personal information if: (a) you contest the accuracy of the data; (b) the processing is unlawful but you oppose deletion; (c) we no longer need the data but you require it for legal claims; or (d) you have objected to processing and we are verifying whether our legitimate grounds override yours.

portability.heading: Data Portability
portability.body: Where processing is based on your consent or on a contract and is carried out by automated means, you have the right to receive the personal information you provided to us in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format, and you have the right to transmit that data to another controller without hindrance from us.

howToExercise.heading: How to Exercise Your Rights
howToExercise.contactIntro: To exercise any of these rights, please contact us at:
howToExercise.name: Atelier Belli — Privacy Department
howToExercise.responseNote: We will respond to your request within the legally required timeframe. We may need to verify your identity before processing your request.
howToExercise.disclaimer: Please note that these rights are not absolute and may be subject to certain exemptions under applicable law.

hero.lede: Savely keeps your money on your phone and nowhere else. If a total reads wrong, a goal will not budge, or a reminder never arrives, write in. Every message is read by the person who built the app.

contact.sub: There is no account to look up and no server to check, so the quickest route is simply telling us what you saw.

email.label: Email
email.hint: The main desk. Write any time.

bug.label: Report a bug
bug.hint: What you tapped, what happened, a screenshot if you have one.

feature.label: Request a feature
feature.hint: Savely is version 1.0. A lot is still open.

security.label: Security concern
security.hint: Tell us privately first, so it is fixed before it is public.

faq.sub: The ones that come up most. If yours is not here, just write.

items.q: Where does my money data live?
items.aHtml: On this iPhone, in a private store only Savely can open. There is no account, no cloud copy, and no connection to anything outside the phone. The app says so itself under Me → Data & privacy: your data never leaves this iPhone. The camera is the only permission it ever asks for, and that is for reading receipts.

items.q: If I lose my phone, can I get my data back?
items.aHtml: Not from us, and we would rather be blunt about it. Nothing is ever uploaded, so there is no copy on our side to restore and no account to recover. What does protect you is your iPhone's own backup: Savely stores everything in the app's normal storage, so it travels with an iCloud or computer backup and returns when you restore a phone. That is the honest trade for keeping your finances off the internet.

items.q: How does the receipt scanner work?
items.aHtml: Point the camera at a receipt and iOS reads it on the device, in Spanish or in English. Nothing is uploaded, and the photo itself is never saved. What you get back is a draft: the amount, the merchant, the date and the category are all editable, and nothing is recorded until you tap Save. You can also pick an existing photo from your library instead.

items.q: What does Auto-move on payday actually do?
items.aHtml: Less than the name promises, and you should know that before you rely on it. Nothing moves on a schedule and nothing runs in the background. You switch it on for a goal, and then, when you log income, Savely may offer to move one amount into that goal. It happens only if you say yes, and the deposit is written together with that income.

items.q: Can I export my data, or erase it?
items.aHtml: There is one export, the Weekly PDF report row under Me → Data & privacy. It covers the current week of income and expenses and hands you a PDF through the share sheet, so treat it as something to read rather than a backup to restore from. To erase, use Delete all data in the same place: every income, expense and goal is removed from this iPhone, your name and reminder settings stay, and it cannot be undone.

cta.sub: Write to us directly. Real replies, patient answers.
cta.label: ivanlorenzana@outlook.com

hero.lede: Fingo is a small app for settling who pays, who goes first, who picks the music. It runs entirely on your phone, with no account and no internet. If something misbehaves, write to us. A real person reads every message.

contact.sub: Three ways in, all of them landing on the same desk.

email.label: Email
email.hint: The main desk. Write any time.

bug.label: Report a bug
bug.hint: A short note and a screenshot go a long way.

feature.label: Request a feature
feature.hint: We read all of them. Some ship.

faq.sub: The ones that come up most. If yours is not here, just write.

items.q: Does Fingo need an account, or the internet?
items.aHtml: Neither. There is no sign-in and no networking code in the app at all, so it behaves exactly the same in airplane mode. It asks for no permissions, collects nothing, and your wheels are saved only on the phone. Delete the app and nothing is left behind.

Four things, one per tab. Chooser picks a finger: everyone holds the screen, and with two or more fingers down a short countdown runs before one is chosen, up to five at a time. Roulette spins a wheel you built yourself. Random gives you a number inside a range you set. Coin Flip is heads or tails.

items.q: I deleted a roulette and it came back. Why?
items.aHtml: So the tab is never empty. If you delete every wheel, Fingo puts the starter one back the next time you open the app: My First Roulette, with the options Yes, No and Maybe. Edit it into something you actually want and it will stay that way.

items.q: Can I turn the vibration off?
items.aHtml: Not inside Fingo today. The app has no settings screen at all, so haptics stay on wherever they fire. If you want a switch for it, write to us and say so.

items.q: Can I save or share a result?
items.aHtml: No, and nothing is kept. A roulette winner appears in a card you dismiss by tapping the background around it, the Chooser clears its result after a moment, and no mode keeps a history. Fingo is built to settle the moment and then get out of the way.

hero.lede: Fave is the notebook for everything you try, and it keeps your lists in your own iCloud rather than on our servers. If a poster loads wrong, a list will not sync, or something simply confuses you, write to us.

contact.sub: There is no account for us to look up, so tell us what you saw and where you saw it.

email.label: Email
email.hint: The main desk. Write any time.

sync.label: iCloud and syncing
sync.hint: Tell us what Profile → Your data shows.

artwork.label: Artwork or titles
artwork.hint: Films and shows come from TMDB, books from Open Library.

bug.label: Report a bug
bug.hint: What you tapped, what happened, a screenshot if you have one.

faq.sub: The ones that come up most. If yours is not here, just write.

items.aHtml: Not with us. Fave has no sign-up, no password and no profile to fill in. Your lists are kept on your iPhone and mirrored to your own private iCloud, so they follow you to a new phone without us ever holding a copy. We cannot read them, and there is nothing on our side to log into.

items.q: What if I am not signed into iCloud?
items.aHtml: Fave still works, it simply cannot carry anything across. Profile → Your data tells you which situation you are in: when there is no iCloud account on the phone it says your lists live only there, and that signing in from Settings will let them keep themselves. Nothing is lost in the meantime.

items.q: What does Fave send to the internet?
items.aHtml: Only what it needs to put a name and a cover on something. Searching a film or a show sends that text to TMDB along with your language setting; searching a book sends the title or the ISBN to Open Library. Posters and covers are downloaded from those same two services, and Fave will quietly fetch a missing one when you open the app. Your stars, your reactions, your notes and your photos are never sent to either of them.

In two steps, because there are two copies. Deleting the app clears it from that iPhone, but the synced copy stays in your iCloud and would return if you reinstalled. To remove it for good, delete the app and then delete Fave's iCloud data from your iPhone's Settings. Inside the app you can also delete a single list or entry by holding it down, which removes it from all of your devices.

items.q: Can I rank anything, or only films and books?
items.aHtml: Both. Movies, Shows and Books are built in, with a search that fills in the title, the year and the artwork. Everything else goes in lists you make yourself, which come in two kinds: Things for anything you try, and Places for cafés and venues, where a place is scored by the orders you rate inside it. Every entry can take one to five stars, an emoji, a note and one photo, and all four are optional.

cta.sub: Write to us directly. Real replies, patient answers.
cta.label: ivanlorenzana@outlook.com

hero.subtitle: A small <it>atelier</it> for software out of Tijuana. Minimalist form, and the patience to finish things. I design and build iOS apps and the web around them.

workbench.desc: A small, opinionated set. Swift and SwiftUI for the phone; <it>Next.js</it> and TypeScript for the web; Postgres for things that must last. Figma, Xcode, Claude Code — the bench stays tidy.

fingo.descRich: An iOS app for making group decisions instantly — wheels, coins, spinning arrows, tap-to-choose. Fully customizable, with <it>haptics</it> that make each pick feel deliberate. Built with SwiftUI.
fingo.tag: Wheels, coins, haptics — decisions in a tap.

savely.descRich: A local-first savings app. Goals with a real pace, everyday income and expense logging, a receipt scanner that reads on the phone, and a payday auto-move that turns income into savings in one tap. No accounts, no cloud, no bank connections — money data lives on the phone and <it>never leaves it</it>. SwiftUI and SwiftData, submitted to the App Store.
savely.tag: Goals, receipts, payday auto-move — money that never leaves the phone.
savely.galleryCaption: Three real screens, seeded through the app's own DEBUG tour: a goal with its pace, a receipt read on-device — the photo never leaves the phone — and payday's one-tap auto-move into that goal.

mezcal.descRich: Storefront and story for an artisanal mezcal brand out of Oaxaca. A quiet, editorial site built to sell — varieties, origin, direct orders. <it>Hand-built</it> from brand to checkout.
mezcal.tag: An artisanal mezcal brand — storefront and story.

blip.descRich: A live monitor for sealed Pokémon TCG product on Amazon México. It watches price, stock and restocks, then fires an instant push with a one-tap deep-link that fills the cart — <it>you</it> finish the purchase. The edge is legitimate speed: know first, tap first.
blip.tag: Price, stock, restocks — alerted before the swarm.

briefmark.descRich: An iOS app that turns TikTok videos into smart bookmarks. Share a URL and it extracts every recommendation — recipes, movies, books, places — into structured, actionable cards, powered by <it>Claude</it>. SwiftUI on the front, a TypeScript backend behind.

pass.descRich: A serverless platform that issues and updates Apple Wallet passes — gym memberships, loyalty stamp cards — with changes pushed in real time straight to the card. AWS Lambda, DynamoDB and the Apple Wallet web service, <it>end to end</it>.
pass.tag: Apple Wallet passes — issued, updated, alive.

story.problem: A Wallet pass cannot be refreshed from an app. Without Apple's pass web service the card goes stale in the user's Wallet, and a stale card is one they delete.
story.approach: A serverless backend that implements the protocol end to end: device registration, pass versioning, PassKit signing and the push that tells the device to come back for a new version.
story.result: Running in production. Memberships and stamp cards are issued over an API and change on the user's card in real time, without them opening anything.

highlights: The full Apple Wallet web service, not just .pkpass generation
APNs push: the pass updates in place on the card
Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB and S3, deployed with SAM
Issued over an API: gym memberships and loyalty stamp cards

alisio.descRich: An iOS and Apple Watch app for zone training. Pick a zone and your watch <it>taps your wrist</it> the moment you drift out — a workout stays a two-second glance, not a screen you study mid-set. It starts standalone from the watch, mirrors live on iPhone, and keeps every session <it>on-device</it>, no account. Built with SwiftUI and HealthKit.
alisio.tag: Heart-rate zones you feel on your wrist — no screen to study.

story.problem: Training by zone means checking your wrist mid-set. At that pace the number arrives late, and looking for it breaks the effort you were trying to hold.
story.approach: The Watch measures and taps: entering the zone, leaving it, hitting the goal. The iPhone only mirrors what the Watch tracks. Zones come from your own profile (Karvonen over the Tanaka formula), not a generic table.
story.result: Shipped to the App Store. A session runs without looking at a screen: pick a zone and a time, and the rest arrives on your wrist. Everything stays on-device, no account.

highlights: Haptic alerts on entering, leaving and completing the goal
Zones from your profile: Karvonen or Simple (Tanaka 2001 basis)
The Watch starts a session on its own, no iPhone nearby
Profile and history sync between devices; nothing leaves them
alisio.mediaCaption: One live session across both devices: started on the iPhone, measured on the Watch, mirrored back to the phone. See the badge flip as the heart rate drifts out of Zone 2 and returns.
alisio.watchCaption: On the wrist alone: pick a zone with the crown, then the live session — the badge slipping out of zone and back in — through to the goal completed.

fave.descRich: An iOS app for the person who already keeps mental lists of every drink, café and movie she has tried. You make a list for anything, tick things off as you go, and give them stars <it>only when you feel like it</it> — rating is never homework. A café keeps its own orders and scores itself from their average. Movies, shows and books fill in their own artwork from TMDB and Open Library. Everything lives in your private iCloud and nowhere else: no accounts, no analytics, no servers of mine.
fave.tag: Rank the drinks, cafés and movies you try.

vitapath.descRich: An emergency medical-response platform. A patient with a serious condition fires an SOS; the nearest paramedic from a <it>private network</it> is dispatched and tracked live; the patient is routed to the right hospital by insurance, proximity and capability; a hospital console runs dispatch, arrival and reception. Two SwiftUI apps, a React console, and a <it>Spring Boot + PostGIS</it> backend with a real-time emergency state machine.
vitapath.tag: SOS to hospital handoff — dispatched, tracked, routed.

story.problem: In an emergency the minutes go to deciding who responds and where the patient is taken. Send them to a hospital that does not take their insurance, or cannot handle the case, and the transfer happens twice.
story.approach: One emergency state machine in Spring Boot. PostGIS picks the nearest available paramedic with an escalation sweep, STOMP keeps the map and ETA live across all three surfaces, and hospital routing scores insurance, proximity and capability with real driving ETAs from OSRM.
story.result: An MVP verified end to end: SOS, offer, accept, transport, hospital handshake and reception, across two SwiftUI apps and a React console, behind 207 unit tests.

highlights: Geospatial dispatch: PostGIS nearest-N plus an escalation sweep
Realtime over STOMP: map and ETA live on both apps and the console
Hospital routing by insurance, proximity and capability
JWT auth with rotating refresh, and a PHI access audit trail
vitapath.mediaCaption: One real emergency across all three surfaces at the same moment. The offer lands on the paramedic's phone, she accepts, and the console resolves the hospital by insurance and network while the patient watches the same road route close in on her own map.
vitapath.galleryCaption: The patient app: the SOS button, live tracking with the paramedic's real road route and ETA, and the emergency card responders read on arrival.

arrhythmia.titleIt: read the ECG, beat by beat.
arrhythmia.descRich: A web front end for a <it>FastAPI</it> ECG arrhythmia classifier. Upload a WFDB record and it renders the whole signal at once, then classifies every beat by AAMI class (N/S/V/F/Q) with model confidence — drill into any flagged beat in a real 60-second context window. Built to prove a genuine ML pipeline, not a notebook: Next.js and TanStack Query on the front, a FastAPI model service behind.
arrhythmia.tag: Upload an ECG, classify every beat (AAMI).

story.problem: The original was a desktop app that plotted the first four seconds of a record and diagnosed one beat per button press. Worse, it evaluated by mixing patients across the split, which inflates every metric it reported.
story.approach: A windowed feature pipeline (FFT/PSD, wavelets, statistics) around each beat feeds a neural network trained on MIT-BIH, served behind FastAPI. Rebuilt with a leakage-free inter-patient protocol, so the baseline is honest instead of flattering.
story.result: A working demo: upload a WFDB record and read the whole trace at once, with every beat classified into its AAMI class and the model's confidence next to it. 168 tests, and the backend is public.

highlights: 5 AAMI EC57 classes (N/S/V/F/Q) with per-beat confidence
Leakage-free inter-patient evaluation: an honest baseline
The full 30-minute record, not a four-second slice
FastAPI and Next.js, with an explicitly versioned model
arrhythmia.mediaCaption: MIT-BIH record 230: 2,464 beats, 123 flagged, classified against the live model.
arrhythmia.galleryCaption: Uploading the record, and a flagged beat opened in its real 60-second context window.
